title: What AI developers could learn from Charles Bukowski?
content_html:
Published: 27th of July, 2026

Allow me to jump straight in:

now I have become spoiled,
I walked into here tonight expecting
more luck
but the night has been slow.
and rightfully so—
occurrence must precede action,
the tank must refill.

/…/

when the lulls arrive there is
nothing to do but
wait,
do other things.

/…/

there are other things to do.
like now I am going downstairs
to see my wife
and my 6 cats

/…/

it will be all right.
I’m sure it
will.

they might even remember me.

– an excerpt from the "block" by Charles Bukowski.

Charles is describing a writers block. Then he's being wise and self-conscious about it and instead of forcing himself to write more slop (or ill words in his world) he stands up, moves away from his computer notebook and goes downstairs to his wife and 6 cats. He knows this block is temporal and things will – presumably soon – be all right. Actually, he's sure of that.

So why do we, developers supercharged with AI tools, have a sudden urge to spend more time building software than ever? Silicon valley, since its inception, has been obsessed with working crazy hours, or at least that's what successful folks in their autobiographies told us. Charles knew that more output does not equal quality output.

Even before the AI, he was okay to throw away work that didn't cut the mustard 👇🏻

the trash can

this is great, I just wrote two
poems I didn't like.
there is a trash can on this
computer.
I just moved the poems
over
and dropped them into
the trash can.
/…/
it's always better
to reject yourself before
the editors do.
/…/

– an excerpt from "the trash can" by Charles Bukowski.

In a recent discussion between Jaron Lanier (that geeky dreadlocks scientist who also makes music) and Neil deGrasse Tyson (that geeky astrophysicist who wrote a book on that subject for normal people that I still didn't understand), Neil said that he has written around 50,000 lines of code – and spent awful lot of time doing so – which AI models today produce in seconds. Then he said:

If I had access [to AI] back then, I'd probably just spend more time on the beach.

Preach on! But… how come we don't see this happening? Why aren't tech folks sipping tequilas on the beach?

Why are we instead witnessing a 996 phenomenon. Why is there a sudden urge to ship 4,500 PRs per day? How many of those PRs have improved anything for our users (to those lucky enough to have users) or solve "a" problem actual people – not personas – verbally said they have?

Would we be more creative if we wandered off to listen to people about ideas we're trying to build?

But maybe the fact that Bukowski turned his inability to write into a poem about his inability to write, and wrote "the trash can" about poems he deleted…
Maybe that's enough to give us all a FOMO, so I'm off vibe-coding my next zero-time Pulitzer Prize winning startup.

PS: If you enjoyed this read, here's part 2: What AI developers could learn from Ernest Hemingway?

If you enjoyed the "block" or "the trash can", consider buying Betting on the Muse, a collection of poetry and short stories by Charles Bukowski.

content_html_zh:
Published: 27th of July, 2026

请允许我直接跳入：

现在我已经被宠坏了，今晚我走进这里期待更多的运气，但夜晚过得很慢。 理所当然的是——发生必须先于行动，水箱必须重新装满。 /…/当平静到来时，除了等待，别无他法，做其他事情。 /…/还有其他事情要做。 就像现在我要下楼去看我的妻子和我的 6 只猫/…/ 一切都会好的。 我确信会的。 他们甚至可能还记得我。

——摘自查尔斯·布考斯基的《街区》。

查尔斯正在描述作家的瓶颈。 然后他就会明智地、自觉地意识到这一点，不再强迫自​​己写更多的废话（或者在他的世界里说脏话），而是站起来，离开电脑笔记本，下楼到他的妻子和 6 只猫身边。 他知道这个障碍是暂时的，事情很快就会好起来的。 事实上，他对此很确定。

那么，为什么我们这些拥有人工智能工具的开发人员会突然想要花比以往更多的时间来构建软件呢？ 硅谷自诞生以来，就一直痴迷于疯狂工作，或者至少成功人士在自传中是这么告诉我们的。 查尔斯知道更多的产出并不等于高质量的产出。

即使在人工智能出现之前，他也可以扔掉不合格的工作👇🏻

垃圾桶

这太棒了，我刚刚写了两首我不喜欢的诗。 这台计算机上有一个垃圾桶。 我只是把那些诗移过来，扔进了垃圾桶。 /…/ 在编辑之前拒绝自己总是更好。 /…/

——摘自查尔斯·布考斯基的《垃圾桶》。

在最近 Jaron Lanier（那个长着辫子的极客科学家，同时也创作音乐）和 Neil deGrasse Tyson（那个极客天体物理学家，为普通人写了一本我仍然无法理解的主题的书）之间的讨论中，尼尔说他已经编写了大约 50,000 行代码 - 并且花费了大量时间 - 今天的人工智能模型可以在几秒钟内生成这些代码。 然后他说：

如果当时我能够使用人工智能，我可能会花更多时间在海滩上。

继续传教！ 但… 为什么我们没有看到这种情况发生？ 为什么科技人员不在海滩上喝龙舌兰酒？

为什么我们反而目睹了 996 现象？ 为什么突然有每天发 4500 个 PR 的冲动？ 其中有多少 PR 为我们的用户（对于那些足够幸运拥有用户的人）带来了任何改进，或者解决了实际人们（而不是人物角色）口头上所说的“问题”？

如果我们走开去听听人们关于我们正在尝试建立的想法，我们会更有创造力吗？

但也许布考斯基把他无法写作的事实写成一首关于他无法写作的诗，并写了关于他删除的诗的“垃圾桶”…… 也许这足以让我们所有人感到害怕，所以我不再为我的下一个零次普利策奖获奖初创公司进行振动编码。

PS：如果您喜欢这篇文章，请阅读第二部分：人工智能开发人员可以从欧内斯特·海明威那里学到什么？

如果您喜欢“街区”或“垃圾桶”，请考虑购买查尔斯·布考斯基的诗歌和短篇小说集《赌注缪斯》。
